title: Painting Software: 8 Tools for Estimates, Crews and Leads
html:
Painting software has to do three jobs: win the estimate, schedule the crew and get paid. Start with one estimate and job tool such as PaintScout or Jobber. Add Wave or QuickBooks for the books and a free Google Business Profile. Published plans here run from $0 to $299 a month.

A painting job is sold before it is worked. The homeowner gets two or three bids, and the painter who answers fast with a clear proposal usually wins. So painting software is judged on how quickly it turns a walkthrough into a signed estimate.

This guide sorts eight tools by the job each one does. Every price comes from the vendor page linked beside it, read in November 2026, and each tool gets one real limit.

Which painting software handles proposals and crew scheduling?

PaintScout is the painting-specific choice, and Jobber and Housecall Pro are the general apps most painters compare it with. All three cover estimates and scheduling, but they differ on how much painting detail they know.

  • PaintScout: production rate estimating with material lists, interactive proposals with eSignature, deposit and final payment collection, and two-way Google Calendar sync. The Sales plan is $119 a month billed monthly or $99 billed annually. The Operations add-on is $99 monthly or $79 annually, and extra seats are $20 a month each. Limit: the page does not say how many users a plan includes, so confirm seats before you buy.
  • Jobber: online booking, scheduling, quotes, invoices and online payments. Core for one user is $49 a month with no commitment, or $29 billed annually. Limit: extra users are $29 a month each, and quote reviews need a separate Reviews add-on.
  • Housecall Pro: scheduling, dispatch, estimates, invoicing and payments. Basic is $59 a month billed annually for one user, and Essentials is $149 billed annually for five users. Its sales proposal tool sits on the Max plan at $299 a month billed annually. Limit: add-on prices are not published.
ToolBuilt forEntry price shownUsers at that price
PaintScout SalesPainting estimates and proposals$119 monthly, $99 billed annuallyNot stated
Jobber CoreGeneral home services$49 monthly, $29 billed annually1
Housecall Pro BasicGeneral home services$79 monthly, $59 billed annually1
Housecall Pro EssentialsSmall crews$189 monthly, $149 billed annually5

Published list prices from each vendor page, November 2026. Taxes, add-ons and card fees are extra.

Painting crews work in job days, not weekly stops. A kitchen interior might take two days and an exterior might take a week. Look for a scheduler that lets one job span several days and shows which crew leader owns it.

Painting estimates also need square footage, coats, prep and trim. A tool that only takes line items forces you to do that math in a spreadsheet. That is why a painting-specific estimator earns a look, even when it costs more than a general app.

Ask each vendor how a repaint of the same house a year later is handled. A tool that copies the old estimate, colors and square footage saves a surprising amount of time on repeat customers.

Also ask about photo storage. Painters document prep work, damage and finished walls to avoid disputes. Jobber lists unlimited photo and video storage only on its Plus plan, so a photo-heavy crew may outgrow Core.

Which tools keep painting leads from going cold?

A lead tool stores every inquiry and reminds you to follow up. A free CRM such as HubSpot covers this for a small painting company, and Jobber and Workiz fold lead tracking into their job apps.

  • HubSpot CRM: the free plan covers up to 2 users and 1,000 contacts with no time limit. The paid Starter plan is listed at $20 per seat a month, with new-customer pricing of $7 billed annually or $10 billed monthly. Limit: free email sends are capped at 2,000 a month and carry HubSpot branding.
  • Jobber lead tracking: client profiles with job history, a communication history of emails and texts, and tags that mark contacts as leads. Limit: the client features come with the Jobber plan, so you cannot buy them alone.
  • Workiz: scheduling, estimates, invoices and client management on three plans, Standard, Pro and Ultimate. Automations are capped at 5, 10 and 30 across those plans. Limit: the page shows request pricing instead of a price, and the free trial is 7 days.

Speed beats polish at the follow-up stage. Send the proposal the same day as the walkthrough, then set a reminder for three days later. A painter who follows up once usually beats the painter who sends a PDF and waits.

Keep a lost-job reason in the CRM. Price, timing and a competitor are three simple choices. After a month of data you can see whether you lose on price or on speed, and fix the right thing.

Seasonal swings make this more useful. Exterior painting slows in cold months, and a CRM full of past estimates gives you a list of homeowners to call when the schedule opens. That list is worth more than any template.

Tag each lead by job type: interior, exterior, cabinet or commercial. Tags let you send a cabinet special only to cabinet leads, instead of emailing everyone about everything.

Which tools handle painting invoices, deposits and the books?

Wave and QuickBooks Online are the two books tools to compare. Painters often take a deposit before the first coat, so card and bank payment fees matter more here than in a weekly service trade.

  • Wave: Starter is $0 and Pro is $19 a month billed monthly. Both allow unlimited estimates and invoices, and card payments on Starter cost 2.9% plus 60 cents. Limit: it is invoicing and bookkeeping, with no crew scheduling.
  • QuickBooks Online: Simple Start is listed at $38 a month, with a 50% promotion for the first three months. Essentials is $85 for three users, and Plus is $140 for five users with project profitability tracking. Limit: Simple Start allows one user.

A $4,000 interior job paid by card on Wave Starter carries about $116.60 in fees at 2.9% plus 60 cents. Ask clients to pay big invoices by bank transfer when you can, and check each vendor for its bank rate.

Project profitability tracking on QuickBooks Plus matters once you run several jobs at once. It lets you compare what a job earned against what it cost, which a one-user plan cannot do.

Keep deposits separate from income in your books. A deposit taken in winter for a spring exterior is money you still owe in work. Whichever tool you pick, set a rule for how deposits are recorded before the first one arrives.

What does painting software cost for a small crew?

A solo painter can run a working stack for $49 a month, and a multi-crew company can land near $303. These totals add plan fees only, so card fees and taxes come on top.

StackPartsMonthly plan cost
Solo painterJobber Core billed monthly, Wave Starter, HubSpot free CRM, Google Business Profile$49
Two-person crewPaintScout Sales billed monthly, QuickBooks Simple Start at list price$157
Multi-crew companyPaintScout Sales plus Operations billed monthly, QuickBooks Essentials at list price$303

Built from the vendor prices above, November 2026. QuickBooks is shown at list price, before its three-month promotion.

The jump from $49 to $157 buys painting-specific estimates and proposals. Whether that pays off depends on how many bids you send. A painter who sends two bids a week may not need it.

Annual billing lowers the PaintScout figure to $99 for Sales and $79 for Operations. That is a saving, but it ties you to a year, so only prepay once you have used the trial.

What should a painting company ask a vendor before signing?

Ask five questions before you pay, because every one of these tools hides a cost somewhere. The answers decide whether the plan price is the real price.

  • How many seats are included? PaintScout does not state included users on its published plans, and Jobber Core covers one.
  • What does card processing cost? Jobber lists 2.9% plus 30 cents, Housecall Pro lists rates from 2.59%, and Wave lists 2.9% plus 60 cents on Starter.
  • Which features sit behind an add-on? Housecall Pro lists add-ons such as Pipeline and Campaigns without prices.
  • Is there a contract? Jobber offers month-to-month plans with no commitment and discounts for annual prepayment.
  • Can you export your data? Ask for a customer export before you load years of jobs into any tool.

Write the answers in one sheet, one row per vendor. A side-by-side sheet makes the cheapest tool and the best fit visible at the same time, and they are often different tools.

Trials help here. PaintScout lists a 14-day trial with no card, Jobber lists 14 days with no card required, and Housecall Pro lists 14 days with no card. Use two real estimates during the trial, not a demo job.

How do painters get found before they ever open the software?

Painters get found through Google Maps, reviews and a clear website. Google says you can add or claim your business at no charge, per its own help page.

  • Google Business Profile: shows your painting company in Maps and local search with photos, reviews, service area and phone number. Limit: it needs fresh job photos and replies to reviews to hold its place.

Before you reply to a bad review, read how to handle a negative review .

A painter site needs pages for interior, exterior and cabinet work, plus a quote form.

How do you choose painting software for your crew?

Choose painting software with a three-check filter: fit, cost and setup effort. Run every tool through all three before you pay.

Fit: does it price by square foot and coats, send a proposal with eSignature, and collect a deposit?

Cost: add the plan price, extra seats, add-ons and card fees, then compare the total against one average interior job.

Setup effort: can you load your price rates and a proposal template in a weekend, or does it need training?

A solo painter should start with Jobber Core or a free CRM, Wave Starter and a free Google Business Profile. That is the whole stack. Upgrade only when you lose bids because proposals go out late.

A crew of five or more fits PaintScout or Housecall Pro Essentials, with QuickBooks for the books. Run the free trial on two real bids before you commit, since the proposal is the part customers see.

Software does not create demand, so pair it with lead sources. Ads from painter Google Ads and rankings from painter SEO send homeowners to the website. Meta Ads for painters reach them before they search.

What is the best painting software for a small business?

There is no single best tool, because it depends on crew size and how many bids you send. PaintScout is built for painting estimates. Jobber and Housecall Pro are general apps with scheduling and invoicing. Run each free trial on two real bids before you decide.

How much does painting software cost?

Published prices here run from $0 for Wave Starter and the HubSpot free CRM to $299 a month for Housecall Pro Max billed annually. PaintScout lists its Sales plan at $119 a month billed monthly. Card fees, extra seats and add-ons cost more.

Do painters need estimating software or a general job app?

It depends on how you price. If you quote by square foot, coats and prep, a painting-specific estimator saves time. If you quote a flat price per room, a general app such as Jobber is often enough for a small crew.

Does painting software take deposits?

Several tools do. PaintScout lists deposit and final payment collection by card and ACH, and Jobber lists invoices with online payments. Card fees apply. Jobber lists 2.9% plus 30 cents, so compare the processing rate as closely as the plan price.

What should a new painting contractor buy first?

Start with a free Google Business Profile, Wave Starter at $0 for invoices and one estimate tool on a free trial. Add crew scheduling only when jobs overlap. Do not pay for a full suite before you have steady bids to send.

Is Google Business Profile free for painters?

Google states that you can add or claim your business at no charge. It still takes work: photos of finished rooms and exteriors, accurate service areas and replies to every review. Google paid ad products are separate and billed on their own.

-
How many seats are included?
PaintScout does not state included users on its published plans, and Jobber Core covers one.
-
What does card processing cost?
Jobber lists 2.9% plus 30 cents, Housecall Pro lists rates from 2.59%, and Wave lists 2.9% plus 60 cents on Starter.
-
Which features sit behind an add-on?
Housecall Pro lists add-ons such as Pipeline and Campaigns without prices.
-
Is there a contract?
Jobber offers month-to-month plans with no commitment and discounts for annual prepayment.
-
Can you export your data?
Ask for a customer export before you load years of jobs into any tool.
Write the answers in one sheet, one row per vendor. A side-by-side sheet makes the cheapest tool and the best fit visible at the same time, and they are often different tools.
Trials help here. PaintScout lists a 14-day trial with no card, Jobber lists 14 days with no card required, and Housecall Pro lists 14 days with no card. Use two real estimates during the trial, not a demo job.

How do painters get found before they ever open the software?
Painters get found through Google Maps, reviews and a clear website. Google says you can add or claim your business at no charge, per its own help page.
-
Google Business Profile:
shows your painting company in Maps and local search with photos, reviews, service area and phone number. Limit: it needs fresh job photos and replies to reviews to hold its place.
Before you reply to a bad review, read how to handle a negative review .
A painter site needs pages for interior, exterior and cabinet work, plus a quote form.

How do you choose painting software for your crew?
Choose painting software with a three-check filter: fit, cost and setup effort. Run every tool through all three before you pay.
Fit:
does it price by square foot and coats, send a proposal with eSignature, and collect a deposit?
Cost:
add the plan price, extra seats, add-ons and card fees, then compare the total against one average interior job.
Setup effort:
can you load your price rates and a proposal template in a weekend, or does it need training?
A solo painter should start with Jobber Core or a free CRM, Wave Starter and a free Google Business Profile. That is the whole stack. Upgrade only when you lose bids because proposals go out late.
A crew of five or more fits PaintScout or Housecall Pro Essentials, with QuickBooks for the books. Run the free trial on two real bids before you commit, since the proposal is the part customers see.
Software does not create demand, so pair it with lead sources. Ads from painter Google Ads and rankings from painter SEO send homeowners to the website. Meta Ads for painters reach them before they search.
###
What is the best painting software for a small business?
There is no single best tool, because it depends on crew size and how many bids you send. PaintScout is built for painting estimates. Jobber and Housecall Pro are general apps with scheduling and invoicing. Run each free trial on two real bids before you decide.
###
How much does painting software cost?
Published prices here run from $0 for Wave Starter and the HubSpot free CRM to $299 a month for Housecall Pro Max billed annually. PaintScout lists its Sales plan at $119 a month billed monthly. Card fees, extra seats and add-ons cost more.
###
Do painters need estimating software or a general job app?
It depends on how you price. If you quote by square foot, coats and prep, a painting-specific estimator saves time. If you quote a flat price per room, a general app such as Jobber is often enough for a small crew.
###
Does painting software take deposits?
Several tools do. PaintScout lists deposit and final payment collection by card and ACH, and Jobber lists invoices with online payments. Card fees apply. Jobber lists 2.9% plus 30 cents, so compare the processing rate as closely as the plan price.
###
What should a new painting contractor buy first?
Start with a free Google Business Profile, Wave Starter at $0 for invoices and one estimate tool on a free trial. Add crew scheduling only when jobs overlap. Do not pay for a full suite before you have steady bids to send.
###
Is Google Business Profile free for painters?
Google states that you can add or claim your business at no charge. It still takes work: photos of finished rooms and exteriors, accurate service areas and replies to every review. Google paid ad products are separate and billed on their own.
